concepts.def: Compound of only hydrogen and carbon atoms
Saturated hydrocarbon: CnH2n+2, all single bonds
Unsaturated hydrocarbon: CnH2n, has a C=C bond
Has an −OH group: general formula CnH2n+1OH
Mix of hydrocarbons of different chain lengths
Separates crude oil by boiling-point fractions

walkthroughs.body_html:
Carbon can bond to four other atoms — so it forms huge families of molecules.

Each family shares a general formula and reacts in similar ways. That makes organic chemistry feel like a pattern game.

Alkanes: single bonds only (saturated). Methane CH4, ethane C2H6, propane C3H8, butane C4H10.

Alkenes: at least one C=C double bond (unsaturated). Ethene C2H4, propene C3H6.

Alcohols: contain an −OH group. Methanol CH3OH, ethanol C2H5OH.

Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons formed from ancient plankton.

Fractional distillation heats the oil — short chains have low boiling points and rise high in the column; long chains drop out low down. Each fraction is a useful fuel or feedstock.
